display.purpose: Note titles; the Home greeting at 30px.

headline.purpose: View titles; the issue title at 26px and the calendar month at 22px.

title.purpose: Headings inside a note, such as Decisions and Actions.

section.purpose: Section headings in the interface, such as a settings group.

label.purpose: Buttons, tabs, segmented controls, links and the file tree.

caption.purpose: Dates, meta lines, counts and calendar entries, with tabular figures.

mono.purpose: Markdown source, code and file paths only.

shadows.name: lift

shadows.name: composer-focus

shadows.name: segment-selected

shadows.name: pop

shadows.name: scrim

motion.name: ease

motion.name: duration-border
motion.purpose: Border and focus-ring changes, column drop targets and graph highlighting.

motion.name: duration-tooltip
motion.purpose: The data-dot tooltip fading in and rising 4px.

motion.name: duration-panel

motion.name: duration-checklist
motion.purpose: A checklist row taking or losing its pending fill.

motion.name: glow

motion.purpose: The one authored animation: a change's target glows amber once when the review bar moves to it, then keeps its pending marker.

motion.value: transition: none; animation: none; glow target: outline 2px solid #8f5200, outline-offset 3px
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every transition and animation is off, and the glow becomes a static Review Amber outline.

narrative.overview:
Nexus is a desk for a small team's meetings and work. A cool zinc-grey shell holds one floating white work panel, and inside it a note and the issue it mentions sit one click apart. Everything at rest is quiet: hairline borders, small radii, the platform's own type and a single iris-blue accent for what the user can act on or where they are. The one warm colour is amber, and it is lit only while an agent change waits for the user to accept or reject it. When the review is finished, the amber goes out.

This is a dense working surface in the manner of Linear for the board, Notion or Obsidian for notes and Temporal for the calendar and shell, borrowing their behaviours and none of their branding. Density comes from 13px controls and 14px text on a fixed ramp; calm comes from tonal layering and restraint rather than decoration. The AI is treated like any other part of the workspace: an answer sits on the same white panel, in the same type, with its citations as small iris chips that open the exact heading or issue. Nexus refuses novelty chrome and dark "AI" styling.

This system is a proposal for Will first and then Hein, who owns Nexus's final visual identity, and it can change until both agree. It is recorded from the static wireframe in `wireframe/` (`index.html`, `wireframe.css` and `wireframe.js`), whose `:root` custom properties are the source of the tokens above. It has not yet been applied to the real app in `apps/`. A few values are literals in the stylesheet rather than custom properties (Amber Paper, Lit Iris, Pale Iris and the Review Night set); they are recorded as tokens so the app can adopt them as such. Dark mode is not designed.
keyCharacteristics: A cool zinc shell with one floating white work panel and 1px hairline borders.
One accent, iris, for actions, selection, links and citations.
Amber means "waiting for your decision" and nothing else.
Status reads by glyph shape first and colour second.
The platform system stack in half-step weights, with tabular figures for dates and keys.
Flat at rest; shadows only on things that float or can be picked up.
One authored motion: the amber glow when a change lands.

rules.name: The Amber Lamp Rule
rules.body: Amber is lit only while a change awaits review. It never marks a warning, a priority, a highlight, a hover or the brand. When the last change is accepted or rejected, no amber remains on the screen.

rules.name: The One Iris Rule
rules.body: Iris is the only accent. It marks what acts (primary buttons, the Ask tag), where the user is (the current item, today, the selected result) and what opens elsewhere (links, citations, calendar issue entries). Nothing is iris for decoration.

rules.name: The Glyph-First Status Rule
rules.body: Pebble, Ember and Fern appear only inside small drawn marks: the status ring, a calendar dot or an answer's section marker. They never fill a card, tint a column or colour text. This is what keeps Ember from reading as Review Amber, because the two share a hue.

rules.name: The Operate Stack Rule
rules.body: Screens people work in, the app and this wireframe, use the platform stack above and ship no web font. This rule does not extend to a landing page, the submission video or any other brand surface, which should source its own display face.

rules.name: The Half-Step Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy moves in half steps: 400 for reading, 500 for sidebar labels and chips, 550 for controls and emphasis, 600 for section headings and the current sidebar item, and 650 for titles, keys and tags. 700 appears only on the letter inside a tile or an avatar.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Dates, times, counts and issue keys use tabular figures, so columns of dates and keys line up.

rules.name: The Bar Never Covers Rule
rules.body: While a review is open, the panel's bottom margin grows by the review bar's measured height plus 20px, and the month grid shrinks its rows to match, so the review bar never covers content.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separate with a Hairline border or a step to the Well before reaching for a shadow. A shadow means the thing floats or moves.

rules.name: The Night Overlay Rule
rules.body: Dark surfaces are for things that float above the work and then leave: the review bar in Review Night, and the tooltip and toast in Graphite. The work panel and everything on it stay light.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: The glow is the only authored animation. Everything else is a state change of 120–250ms on the ease-out curve.

dos: **Do** mark every pending value in three ways: an Amber Wash fill with an Amber Hairline border, a "Pending review" or "Pending" tag, and screen-reader text. Show the value it replaces beside it, struck through.
**Do** show one pending change everywhere its item appears (the note, the issue, the board card and the calendar entry), so the user can decide where it applies.
**Do** pair each status colour with its ring shape (empty, half-filled, filled with a check), so status reads without colour.
**Do** separate with a 1px Hairline (#e4e4ea) or the Well (#f7f7f9) before using a shadow.
**Do** give every interactive element a 2px Iris outline at a 2px offset on focus, and Pale Iris (#aab0ff) on the review bar.
**Do** keep notes and issue descriptions to a 68ch measure, and check every view at 390px.
**Do** draw icons as SVG on a 24px grid with a 1.75 stroke and round caps and joins.
donts: **Don't** use amber for anything except a change awaiting review (not for warnings, priority, highlights or hover), and don't let Ember leave the In progress ring.
**Don't** give the AI its own look. Ask answers get no dark panels, gradients, glows, sparkles or special type; they sit on the white panel like a note.
**Don't** add novelty chrome: gradient text, glass or blur, ornament or decorative illustration. The graph's dot grid is the one patterned surface, because it is a canvas for placed nodes.
**Don't** add a second accent, or use Lagoon or Heather for actions; they name events and projects only.
**Don't** fill cards, columns or rows with a status colour; status lives in the ring.
**Don't** use monospace except for Markdown source, code and file paths.
**Don't** put a label or eyebrow above a heading, or use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons.
**Don't** make the work panel dark or derive a dark theme by inverting these tokens; dark mode is not designed yet.
